theorem:little1.paper_reading: Consider a LIFO queueing system equipped with a finite set B of buffer locations (of cardinality |B|), where each buffer location holds at most one job at any time and a job entering a buffer location b in B remains in that same location b until it departs. Let N(t) be the cumulative number of arrivals up to time t that occupy a buffer location in B, let D(t) be the cumulative number of departures up to time t from buffer locations in B, and let W_i be the delay (time from arrival to departure) of the i-th job to depart from B. Assume there exists a strictly positive constant lambda_min > 0 such that, with probability 1, liminf_{t -> infinity} N(t)/t >= lambda_min, and further assume that, with probability 1, lim_{t -> infinity} D(t) = infinity (infinitely many departures occur from B). Then with probability 1, the limsup average delay over departing jobs, W_bar := limsup_{t -> infinity} (1 / D(t)) * sum_{i=1}^{D(t)} W_i, satisfies W_bar <= |B| / lambda_min.
theorem:little1.lean_reading: For any finite type B (with cardinality |B| = Fintype.card B), arbitrary job index type ι, probability space (Ω, μ), sample-path family sys : Ω → BufferSystem B ι, and real constant lamMin > 0: where each BufferSystem assigns every job k a discrete arrival slot arrival k : ℕ, a departure slot depart k : WithTop ℕ (⊤ meaning never departs) with arrival k ≤ depart k, a fixed buffer slot slot k : B, finitely many arrivals before every horizon t, and single-occupancy disjointness of half-open residency intervals [arrival k, depart k) within each slot b ∈ B; define N(t) = |{k | arrival k < t}|, D(t) = |{k | depart k ≤ t}|, jobDelay k = d - arrival k when depart k = some d (and 0 if ⊤), and avgDelay t = (∑_{k : depart k ≤ t} jobDelay k) / D(t). If μ-almost surely liminf_{t → ∞} (N(t) / t : EReal) ≥ lamMin and D(t) → ∞ as t → ∞, then μ-almost surely limsup_{t → ∞} (avgDelay t : EReal) ≤ (|B| / lamMin : EReal).

analysis.summary: LifoBackpressure.Statements.Theorem1Statement matches Paper Theorem 1 (theorem:little1) across all 7 numbered obligations (C1-C7) in the paper's slotted discrete-time setting. It formalizes the fixed-slot single-occupancy buffer discipline on a finite slot set B, keeps both almost-sure hypotheses (liminf N(t)/t >= lambda_min > 0 and D(t) -> infinity), and concludes the exact almost-sure delay upper bound limsup avgDelay(t) <= |B| / lambda_min. The only modeling choice is fixing discrete time t in N (matching Section III and Theorem 4) rather than the continuous-time integral notation written in Appendix A.

cases.case: C1: Finite buffer set B and probability space
cases.paper: Finite set B of buffer locations with cardinality |B| on a probability space (L517, L530).

cases.case: C2: Arrival count N(t), departure count D(t), delays W_i, and empirical average delay
cases.paper: N(t) arrivals into B up to time t; D(t) departures from B up to time t; W_i delay of i-th departing job; W_bar := limsup_{t -> infinity} (1 / D(t)) sum_{i=1}^{D(t)} W_i (L518-L522, L529).
cases.lean: arrivalsCount t = |{k | arrival k < t}|, departuresCount t = |{k | depart k <= t}|, totalDelay t = sum_{k : depart k <= t} jobDelay k, avgDelay t = totalDelay t / departuresCount t, and Filter.limsup (fun t => (avgDelay t : EReal)) Filter.atTop.
cases.why: Using arrival < t (slots 0..t-1) and depart <= t aligns with discrete t-slot horizon sums (any job arriving before t and not departing by t occupies a slot at time t, so D(t) >= N(t) - |B|, and every job departing by t has occupancy interval inside [0, t)). Shifting t by 1 leaves liminf N(t)/t and limsup avgDelay(t) unchanged.

cases.paper: Each slot b in B has occupancy Q^(b)(t) in {0, 1}, and a job entering slot b stays in b until departure, giving D(t) >= N(t) - |B| (L217, L1024-L1029, L1072-L1073).

theorem:qla-markovian.paper_reading: Under the Section III discrete-time stochastic network model (r >= 1 queues, finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov chain S(t) with stationary distribution pi > 0, time-invariant compact feasible action sets X^(s_i), continuous time-invariant cost f >= 0, arrival A_j >= 0, and service mu_j >= 0 uniformly bounded by delta_max in (0, infinity), queue dynamics q_j(t+1) = max[q_j(t) - mu_j(t), 0] + A_j(t) with q(0) = 0) and the Slater eta-slackness condition (eq:slackness), Backpressure (eq:QLAeq, with either FIFO or LIFO discipline) for control parameter V >= 1 achieves expected time-average cost f_av^BP = f_av^* + O(1/V) (where f_av^* is the optimal time-average cost over all feasible stable policies) and expected time-average total backlog q_bar^BP = O(V) (in particular, Backpressure is stable).
theorem:qla-markovian.lean_reading: For any NetworkModel M (finite nonempty decidable State, r > 0 queues, irreducible aperiodic stochastic transition matrix P with strictly positive stationary distribution π, compact nonempty topological Action s per state, continuous cost, arrival, and service functions valued in [0, δmax] for δmax > 0) and η : ℝ satisfying M.HasSlackness η (η > 0 and a finite Fin m convex combination of actions per state with stationary expected drift A_j - μ_j <= -η on every queue j): there exist nonnegative constants C_cost, C_q0, C_q1 independent of V, the probability space (Ω, μ), the MarkovProcess realization proc of S(t), and the policy pol, such that for all V >= 1 and every measurable Policy pol on proc satisfying pol.FollowsBackpressure V (governed by a deterministic state-backlog maximizer choice(s, q) of -V f(s, x) + sum_j q_j (μ_j(s, x) - A_j(s, x))), pol is stable (pol.avgBacklog < ⊤), M.optCost proc <= pol.avgCost, pol.avgCost <= M.optCost proc + (C_cost / V : EReal), and pol.avgBacklog <= (C_q0 + C_q1 * V : EReal), where optCost is the EReal infimum of avgCost over all measurable (possibly non-causal) stable policies on proc.
theorem:qla-markovian.lean_refs: lean/Statements/MarkovTradeoff.lean:L14-L29 (Theorem2Statement); lean/Statements/SystemModel.lean:L17-L208 (matPow, Irreducible, Aperiodic, NetworkModel, HasSlackness, queueNext, MarkovProcess, Policy, Policy.queue, Policy.avgBacklog, Policy.IsStable, Policy.avgCost, optCost, IsBackpressureRule, Policy.FollowsBackpressure)
theorem:qla-markovian.stronger_result: M.optCost proc takes the infimum over all measurable (including non-causal/clairvoyant) stable policies on proc rather than only causal policies, making pol.avgCost <= M.optCost proc + C_cost / V at least as strong as the causal-policy benchmark; moreover, the constants C_cost, C_q0, C_q1 are uniform across all V >= 1, initial state distributions of S(0), probability spaces (Ω, μ), and Backpressure tie-breaking rules.

analysis.summary: LifoBackpressure.Statements.Theorem2Statement matches Paper Theorem 2 (theorem:qla-markovian) across all 10 numbered obligations (C1-C10), with uniform V-independent [O(1/V), O(V)] cost and backlog bounds and explicit stability. Minor modeling normalizations are cleanly recorded: NetworkModel fixes the primary nonnegative cost-minimization setting f in [0, delta_max] (omitting the parenthetical reward-maximization sign convention f in [-delta_max, 0], which reduces by shifting f by +delta_max), makes Nonempty (Action s) explicit, uses a finite convex combination in HasSlackness (equivalent to Eq. (2)'s countable series by compactness and Caratheodory's theorem), fixes deterministic state-backlog tie-breaking in FollowsBackpressure, and benchmarks against all measurable (possibly non-causal) stable policies in optCost (which strengthens the cost upper bound).

cases.case: C4: Queue dynamics with q(0) = 0
cases.lean: Policy.queue 0 ω = 0 and Policy.queue (t+1) ω = queueNext (pol.queue t ω) (M.service ...) (M.arrival ...), where queueNext q μ A j = max (q j - μ j) 0 + A j.

cases.case: C5: Slater eta-slackness condition (Eq. 2)
cases.paper: Countable collection {x^(s_i)k}_{k=1..infinity} with weights theta^(s_i)_k >= 0 summing to 1 and stationary expected drift <= -eta for some eta > 0 (L300-L305, L541).
cases.lean: NetworkModel.HasSlackness η uses a finite index Fin m per state with weights θ s k >= 0 summing to 1 and stationary expected drift <= -η.
cases.why: Mathematically equivalent to the paper's countable series: since Action s is compact and arrival - service is continuous, its image K_s in R^r is compact, so conv(K_s) is compact and by Caratheodory's theorem every countable convex combination equals a finite convex combination of at most r + 1 actions.

cases.case: C6: Backpressure policy (Eq. 6) under FIFO or LIFO
cases.paper: At each slot t, choose x^(S(t)) maximizing -V f(s_i, x) + sum_j q_j(t) (mu_j(s_i, x) - A_j(s_i, x)), with either FIFO or LIFO queueing discipline (L430-L435, L541).
cases.lean: Policy.FollowsBackpressure V pol asserts existence of a deterministic state-backlog rule choice(s, q) satisfying IsBackpressureRule V choice such that pol.act t ω = choice (proc.S t ω) (pol.queue t ω).
cases.why: Matches Eq. (6) and covers both FIFO and LIFO because aggregate backlog q(t) is identical under both disciplines; fixes tie-breaking to a deterministic time-homogeneous function choice(s, q) of current state and backlog.

cases.case: C7: Definitions of avgCost, avgBacklog, stability, and optimal stable cost f_av^*

cases.lean: Policy.avgBacklog, Policy.IsStable := avgBacklog < ⊤, Policy.avgCost, and M.optCost proc := iInf over all measurable stable Policy proc (without requiring causal adaptedness).
cases.why: Exact formulas for Eqs. (4)-(5). Allowing arbitrary measurable (even non-causal/clairvoyant) policies in Policy enlarges the comparison class, making M.optCost proc <= causal optCost and thereby strengthening pol.avgCost <= M.optCost proc + C_cost / V.

cases.lean: M.optCost proc ≤ pol.avgCost ∧ pol.avgCost ≤ M.optCost proc + ((C_cost / V : ℝ) : EReal).

cases.paper: q_bar^BP = O(V) and Backpressure is stable (L543, L320-L323).
cases.lean: pol.IsStable ∧ pol.avgBacklog ≤ ((C_q0 + C_q1 * V : ℝ) : EReal).
cases.why: Exact match: for V >= 1, C_q0 + C_q1 * V <= (C_q0 + C_q1) * V, giving q_bar^BP = O(V) and explicit finiteness pol.avgBacklog < ⊤.

thm:prob_multi_con.paper_reading: Under the Section III–V stochastic network model (finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov chain S(t), compact X^(s_i), delta_max-bounded continuous f, A_j, mu_j, queue dynamics eq:queuedynamic with q(0) = 0) and Backpressure (eq:QLAeq, FIFO or LIFO), suppose the optimal dual multiplier gamma_V^* >= 0 of max_{gamma >= 0} g(gamma) (eq:dualproblem, eq:dual_separable) is unique, Slater eta-slackness (eq:slackness) holds, and g(gamma_V^*) >= g(gamma) + L ||gamma_V^* - gamma|| for all gamma >= 0 with a constant L > 0 independent of V (Euclidean norm). Then there exist constants D, K, c^* = Theta(1) (positive finite constants independent of V and m) such that for all m >= 0, P^(r)(D, K m) := limsup_{t->inf} (1/t) sum_{tau=0}^{t-1} Pr{exists j, |q_j(tau) - gamma_{Vj}^*| > D + K m} <= c^* e^{-m}.
thm:prob_multi_con.lean_reading: For any NetworkModel M, η : ℝ with M.HasSlackness η, and L > 0: there exist strictly positive constants D, K, cstar > 0 (depending only on M, η, L, and independent of V, γstar, Ω, μ, proc, pol, and m) such that for every V >= 1, every γstar : Fin M.r → ℝ satisfying M.IsUniqueDualOpt V γstar and M.DualPolyhedral V γstar L (meaning g(V, γ) + L * eucDist γstar γ <= g(V, γstar) for all γ >= 0, where g(V, γ) = sum_s π_s * inf_{x ∈ Action s} (V f(s, x) + sum_j γ_j (A_j(s, x) - μ_j(s, x)))), every probability space (Ω, μ), MarkovProcess proc, Backpressure policy pol (pol.FollowsBackpressure V), and real m >= 0, the EReal time-average deviation probability deviationProb pol γstar D (K * m) := limsup_{t → ∞} (1/t) sum_{τ < t} (μ {ω | ∃ j, D + K * m < |pol.queue τ ω j - γstar j|}).toReal is at most (cstar * Real.exp (-m) : EReal).

thm:qlalifo_delay.paper_reading: Under the Section III–V stochastic network model running LIFO-Backpressure, suppose V >= 1, gamma_V^* is unique, Slater slackness (eq:slackness) holds, g(gamma_V^*) >= g(gamma) + L ||gamma_V^* - gamma|| for all gamma >= 0 with L > 0 independent of V, and time averages under Backpressure exist with probability 1 (and equal their limiting expectations in the proof's DCT step). Let D, K, c^* = Theta(1) be the constants from Theorem 3, Q_{j,High} := gamma_{Vj}^* + D + K [log(V)]^2, Q_{j,Low} := max[gamma_{Vj}^* - D - K [log(V)]^2, 0], and B_j := [Q_{j,Low}, Q_{j,High}] (endpoints reversed as a typo at L605/L664). For any queue j with time-average arrival rate lambda_j > 0: (a) the rate lambda_tilde_j of packets arriving when q_j(t) in B_j that eventually depart satisfies lambda_j >= lambda_tilde_j >= [lambda_j - delta_max c^* / V^{log(V)}]^+; (b) the average delay of these packets is at most W_bound := [2 D + 2 K [log(V)]^2 + delta_max] / lambda_tilde_j.
thm:qlalifo_delay.lean_reading: For any NetworkModel M, η : ℝ with M.HasSlackness η, and L > 0: there exist strictly positive constants D, K, cstar > 0 independent of V, γstar, Ω, μ, proc, pol, j, and the packet realization such that for every V >= 1, every γstar satisfying M.IsUniqueDualOpt V γstar and M.DualPolyhedral V γstar L, every probability space (Ω, μ), MarkovProcess proc, Backpressure policy pol (pol.FollowsBackpressure V), queue j : Fin M.r, discrete unit-packet LIFO buffer realization Q : LifoQueueRealization pol j ι (integer packet arrivals matching M.arrival, fixed nonnegative integer slots with max(q_j(τ) - δmax, 0) <= slot < q_j(τ) + δmax, disjoint slot occupancy, never-departing count <= q_j(τ), and measurability of never-departing count), and deterministic reals lamJ > 0 and lamTilde to which the full arrival rate and in-window arrival rate (with backlogWindow = [qLow, qHigh]) converge μ-almost surely: (a) the arrival rate of in-window eventually-departing packets converges μ-almost surely to lamTilde, and max(lamJ - M.δmax * cstar / V^(Real.log V), 0) <= lamTilde <= lamJ; (b) assuming additionally 0 < lamTilde, the limsup average delay of Q.windowBufferSystem (restricted to in-window eventually-departing packets) satisfies limsup avgDelay(t) <= ((2 * D + 2 * K * (Real.log V)^2 + 2 * M.δmax + 1) / lamTilde : EReal) μ-almost surely.
thm:qlalifo_delay.lean_refs: lean/Statements/LifoDelay.lean:L19-L172 (qHigh, qLow, backlogWindow, LifoQueueRealization, windowDepartingSet, windowDepartingArrivals, enlargedBufferSlots, windowBufferSystem, Theorem4Statement); lean/Statements/Little.lean:L15-L77; lean/Statements/SystemModel.lean:L17-L208
thm:qlalifo_delay.issue: Theorem4Statement formalizes the clean, mathematically sound version of Theorem 4 and therefore differs from the printed manuscript in five concrete ways (one coarser constant in Part (b) plus four missing hypotheses/corrections): (1) Part (b)'s numerator is 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1 rather than the paper's 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + delta_max, because under Eq. (3) service up to delta_max occurs before arrivals so arriving packets can enter slots as low as max(Q_{j,Low} - delta_max, 0) (adding +delta_max to the buffer window width) and discrete integer slot counting adds at most +1; (2) Part (b) adds the explicit guard 0 < lamTilde (omitted in the paper, where V >= 1 alone allows lamTilde = 0 and division by zero in W_bound); (3) Lean assumes a.s.-constant deterministic time-average arrival rates lamJ and lamTilde (whereas L593 only states that time averages exist a.s., which is insufficient for the DCT step equating sample-path averages to expectations at L641-L648); (4) Lean adds an explicit discrete unit-packet LifoQueueRealization coupling packets and integer slots to real-valued Eq. (3) dynamics; and (5) Lean corrects the reversed-endpoint typo B_j = [Q_{j,High}, Q_{j,Low}] at L605/L664 to [Q_{j,Low}, Q_{j,High}].
thm:qlalifo_delay.next: Review the five mathematical discrepancies and record synchronized manuscript revision suggestions in manuscript-edits.json (updating W_bound to include +2*delta_max + 1 under Eq. (3) or explicitly adopting arrivals-before-service dynamics, adding the lambda_tilde_j > 0 guard in Part (b), stating a.s.-constant/ergodic time averages at L593, stating the integer-packet LIFO slot model, and reversing the endpoint typos at L605 and L664), then confirm whether Theorem4Statement is the desired target statement for formal verification.

analysis.summary: LifoBackpressure.Statements.Theorem4Statement intentionally formalizes the mathematically sound version of Paper Theorem 4 (thm:qlalifo_delay) across all 11 numbered obligations (C1-C11), exposing genuine gaps and a constant error in the printed manuscript. Part (a) matches the paper's rate bounds verbatim once a.s.-constant time averages (C5) and a discrete unit-packet LIFO realization (C7) are added and the reversed-endpoint typo at L605 is corrected (C4). Part (b) adds the missing guard 0 < lamTilde (C8) to avoid division by zero when V >= 1 is small, and proves the coarser bound (2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1) / lamTilde instead of the paper's (2D + 2K[log V]^2 + delta_max) / lamTilde (C11, weaker conclusion) because Eq. (3) serves up to delta_max packets before arrivals—shifting the bottom reachable buffer slot down by delta_max—and discrete integer slot counting adds up to +1. Both bounds have the same O([log V]^2 / lamTilde) asymptotic order, but because C11 has a strictly larger numerator, the comparison result is recorded as difference for author review and manuscript revision tracking.

cases.case: C3: Unique dual optimum, Slater eta-slackness, and V-independent polyhedral dual growth
cases.paper: Unique gamma_V^*, eta-slackness (Eq. 2), and g(gamma_V^*) >= g(gamma) + L ||gamma_V^* - gamma|| for all gamma >= 0 with L > 0 independent of V (L611-L617).

cases.case: C4: Constants D, K, c^* and backlog window B_j
cases.paper: D, K, c^* = Theta(1) from Theorem 3; Q_{j,High} = gamma_{Vj}^* + D + K[log V]^2, Q_{j,Low} = max[gamma_{Vj}^* - D - K[log V]^2, 0], and B_j := [Q_{j,High}, Q_{j,Low}] (reversed endpoints at L605/L664; corrected to [Q_{j,Low}, Q_{j,High}] at L652).

cases.case: C5: Almost-sure constancy (ergodicity) of time-average arrival rates
cases.paper: L593 assumes only that time averages under Backpressure exist with probability 1, yet L641-L648 invokes DCT to equate the a.s. sample-path average to the limiting expectation.
cases.lean: Explicitly takes deterministic constants lamJ, lamTilde : ℝ and assumes the full arrival rate converges a.s. to lamJ and the in-window arrival rate converges a.s. to lamTilde.
cases.why: Without a.s. constancy (ergodicity), a random a.s. limit X(ω) only satisfies E[X] = lim (1/t) sum E[...], not X(ω) = lim (1/t) sum E[...] a.s. Lean adds the exact deterministic-limit hypothesis needed to make the proof valid.

cases.case: C6: Positive time-average input rate lambda_j > 0 for queue j
cases.paper: For any queue j with time-average input rate lambda_j > 0 (L587-L591, L618).
cases.lean: ∀ (j : Fin M.r) ... (lamJ : ℝ), 0 < lamJ and a.s. convergence of (1/t) sum_{τ < t} A_j(τ) to lamJ.
cases.why: Exact correspondence (with a.s. constancy tracked separately in C5).

cases.case: C7: Discrete unit-packet LIFO buffer realization
cases.paper: Section III defines real-valued A_j, mu_j, q_j in R_+, while L205, L217, L594, and L664-L665 informally treat packets as unit-sized discrete jobs occupying fixed LIFO buffer slots so Theorem 1 applies.
cases.lean: Explicitly quantifies over a LifoQueueRealization pol j ι coupling discrete packets (arrival, depart, integer slot) to M.arrival and pol.queue via arrivals_at_eq, slot_bounds (max(q_j(τ) - δmax, 0) <= slot < q_j(τ) + δmax), disjoint_slots, never_depart_le_queue, and measurable_never_depart.
cases.why: Makes explicit the unstated discrete unit-packet LIFO slot model required to define individual packet delays and invoke Theorem 1.

cases.case: C8: Missing positivity guard lambda_tilde_j > 0 in Part (b)
cases.paper: Theorem 4 states Part (b) without requiring lambda_tilde_j > 0, even though V >= 1 allows lambda_j - delta_max * c^* / V^{log V} <= 0 and lambda_tilde_j = 0, causing division by zero in W_bound (L624, L628).
cases.lean: Explicitly guards Part (b) with 0 < lamTilde →.
cases.why: Necessary for well-definedness of W_bound and to satisfy Theorem 1's strict positivity hypothesis lambda_min > 0 (and guarantee infinitely many departures).

cases.case: C9: Part (a) identification of lambda_tilde_j and upper bound lambda_tilde_j <= lambda_j
cases.paper: The rate lambda_tilde_j of packets arriving when q_j(t) in B_j that eventually depart satisfies lambda_tilde_j <= lambda_j (L621-L624).
cases.lean: Concludes both ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun t => Q.windowDepartingArrivals / t) atTop (nhds lamTilde) and lamTilde <= lamJ.
cases.why: Exact match (and explicitly confirms the paper's claim at L637-L638 that the eventually-departing in-window rate equals the total in-window arrival rate).

cases.case: C10: Part (a) lower bound lambda_tilde_j >= [lambda_j - delta_max c^* / V^{log(V)}]^+
cases.paper: lambda_tilde_j >= [lambda_j - delta_max c^* / V^{log(V)}]^+ (L624).
cases.lean: max (lamJ - M.δmax * cstar / (V ^ Real.log V)) 0 <= lamTilde.
cases.why: Exact match (for V >= 1, V^(Real.log V) = exp((log V)^2) matches e^{-m} at m = [log V]^2).

cases.case: C11: Part (b) average delay bound numerator (+2*delta_max + 1 vs +delta_max)
cases.paper: Average delay of in-window eventually-departing packets is at most [2D + 2K[log(V)]^2 + delta_max] / lambda_tilde_j, asserting |B̃_j| <= 2D + 2K[log(V)]^2 + delta_max for B̃_j = [Q_{j,High} + delta_max, Q_{j,Low}] (L628, L664-L665).
cases.lean: ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Filter.limsup (fun t => ((Q.windowBufferSystem ...).avgDelay t : EReal)) Filter.atTop <= (((2 * D + 2 * K * (Real.log V) ^ 2 + 2 * M.δmax + 1) / lamTilde : ℝ) : EReal).
cases.why: Under Eq. (3) (q_j(t+1) = max(q_j(t) - mu_j(t), 0) + A_j(t)), service mu_j(t) <= delta_max occurs before arrivals A_j(t) <= delta_max, so packets arriving when q_j(t) in [Q_{j,Low}, Q_{j,High}] can land in integer slots down to max(Q_{j,Low} - delta_max, 0) and up to < Q_{j,High} + delta_max. The interval [max(Q_{j,Low} - delta_max, 0), Q_{j,High} + delta_max) has width at most 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max and contains Ceil(b) - Ceil(a) < (b - a) + 1 integer slots, yielding the sound numerator 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1. Note also that while enlargedBufferSlots uses Nat.floor at the lower endpoint, avgDelay is independent of the ambient slot set B, so the proof can invoke Theorem 1 on the tighter subset Ico (Nat.ceil ...) (Nat.ceil ...) of cardinality <= 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1. Because the formalized numerator exceeds the paper's by delta_max + 1, this is a weaker (coarser) constant bound, though still O([log V]^2 / lambda_tilde_j).

analysis.scope: Theorem4Statement captures the complete mathematically sound O([log V]^2) LIFO-Backpressure delay guarantee (Part (a) exact, Part (b) with the sound numerator 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1 under Eq. (3) and explicit 0 < lamTilde guard). It does not prove the printed manuscript's tighter numerator 2D + 2K[log V]^2 + delta_max under Eq. (3), nor does it hold without a.s.-constant time averages, 0 < lamTilde, and a discrete packet realization. All noncomputable definitions are classical analysis/cardinality/measure-theory operations without any algorithmic conflict; all external dependencies are standard Mathlib/Lean packages.

analysis.suggested_feedback: Theorem 4 in the manuscript needs five mathematical clarifications/fixes to match the true statement proved in Lean: (1) under Eq. (3) service-before-arrival dynamics and integer slot rounding, enlarge the buffer window to [max(Q_{j,Low} - delta_max, 0), Q_{j,High} + delta_max) and update W_bound's numerator to 2D + 2K[log(V)]^2 + 2*delta_max + 1; (2) add the hypothesis lambda_tilde_j > 0 to Part (b); (3) strengthen the L593 assumption from 'time averages exist a.s.' to 'time averages exist and are a.s. constant'; (4) state the integer unit-packet LIFO buffer slot assumptions explicitly; and (5) fix the reversed interval endpoints at L605 and L664.
